name: Restricted settings for sideloaded apps
plain: Android blocks some powerful toggles for apps installed outside stores.
meaning: Accessibility, notification listener and similar options are greyed out for sideloaded apps until the person opens App Info and allows restricted settings.

android.api_surface: Not an app API; PackageInstaller sessions mark source
android.note: Android 14 expanded the scope; Android 15 refined for session installers; Android 16 more checks.

ios.permission: None; no sideloading path on most devices

limits.headline: Can't turn on powerful settings for apps installed outside stores until you allow it
limits.user_action: You open App info, tap the menu and choose Allow restricted settings
can: Install outside a store on Android
Ask you to unlock the options in App info
cannot: Use accessibility or notification listener until you allow restricted settings
Do this on iPhone; there is no sideloading path on most devices
limits.differs: Android blocks these toggles for sideloaded apps; iPhone has no equivalent.

story.what_it_is: Android blocks powerful toggles for apps installed from outside the store, until you unlock them on purpose.
story.for_you: If you install an app from a website, some switches look greyed out. You have to open App info and allow restricted settings first. It is a speed bump that makes scammers' lives harder.
story.for_makers: Scammers talk people into installing an app and then turning on accessibility or notification access. Restricted settings adds a step that the scammer cannot complete without you noticing. It is a platform level defense against fraud.

use_cases.example: A fake bank app tries to get accessibility access and is blocked until the user unlocks it.
A scam call tells someone to install a support tool, and the greyed out switch breaks the script.
A company sideloads a work app and has to approve it for settings.
A developer testing an app learns why a setting is greyed out.
A game helper app installed from a website cannot get screen tap control.
An anti malware app uses the same switch to protect the person.
A payment fraud team counts how many cases the block stopped.

risks: Hard to use for legitimate sideloaded apps
Users can be coached around it
story.android_note: Android 14 widened the block, Android 15 changed rules for session installers and Android 16 adds more checks.
